caption:
SET YOUR CORTISOL RHYTHM CORRECTLY: THE KEY TO HAVING A LOT OF NATURAL MORNING “GET UP & GO ENERGY” •
-
There’s a lot to say about cortisol and I’ll cover more in an upcoming podcast, but it’s fair to say that most people would do well to increase the amount of cortisol they secrete into their blood first thing in the morning and decrease the amount in the evening and at night prior to going to sleep.
-
In this post, I explain how to spike your morning cortisol and why that’s a really good thing to do for your overall daytime mood, focus, and alertness, cognition and immune system function, and for limiting nighttime anxiety… and thus making it easier to fall and stay asleep. Anyone dealing with a health challenge of any kind will also benefit from setting their cortisol rhythm correctly.
-
Regardless of when you wake up or go to sleep, the ideal pattern is relatively high cortisol in the 1-2hrs after waking and low in the 1-2 hours prior to sleep.
-
To achieve that you want to do opposite things of the two ends of the day. Bright light, hydration, exercise, caffeine early in the day as soon as possible after waking. And then at night: dim lights, avoiding a bright short wavelength light (not just blue light), avoiding caffeine, etc. 
-
I’ll cover more specifics in an upcoming episode of the Huberman Lab podcast, but this post introduces you to the general contour of what is ideal for your mental health and physical health as it relates to cortisol patterns across the 24 hour cycle and what you can do to impose the best patterns.
-
And of course, nobody’s perfect about this stuff. Strive to do as well as you can most mornings and nights. A late night out (or in) with friends or family is a great thing every once in a while.

Magnesium is involved in over 600 reactions in your body. 

And up to 80% of people may have low levels that never get flagged on a standard blood test.

That’s because standard tests measure serum magnesium just 1% of what’s actually in your body. Your levels can look normal while your tissues are running low. If you want an accurate picture, ask for an RBC magnesium test.

The gap is also getting harder to close through food alone. 

Between 1940 and 1991, magnesium levels in vegetables dropped by 23%. Food processing can remove up to 80% more. Chronic stress, caffeine, and alcohol deplete what’s left.

The form you take matters.

caption:
International travel finally caught up with me, so yesterday became a bone broth day.

After a stretch of flights, time-zone changes, and disrupted sleep, I woke up feeling a little worn down. 

Not terribly sick, but enough that my body was asking for warmth, fluids, and a slower pace.

Bone broth is one of my go-tos on days like this because it’s simple and deeply nourishing. Warm fluids, protein, collagen-derived gelatin, and amino acids like glycine and proline from a long, slow simmer. I also like adding ginger and turmeric for the flavor, warmth, and the anti-inflammatory compounds they contain.

Here’s the version I made:

• 2–3 lbs beef bones, ideally marrow + joint bones
• 3–4 inches fresh ginger, sliced
• 2–3 inches fresh turmeric, sliced
• 2 tbsp apple cider vinegar
• 1 large onion, quartered
• 1 head garlic, halved or smashed
• Optional: carrots + celery
• 1 tbsp whole black peppercorns
• 1–2 bay leaves
• 1 tsp sea salt
• 8–10 cups water, enough to cover everything

Roast the bones at 400°F for 30 minutes, until deeply browned.

Transfer to a slow cooker with the remaining ingredients.

Cover with water and cook on LOW for 12–24 hours.

Strain, cool, skim excess fat if desired, and store in the fridge.

I’ll be sipping this over the next few days while doing the boring-but-important recovery things like sleep, hydration, sunlight, and taking it easy until I feel fully back.

caption:
Muscle loss with age is common, but much of that decline is driven by inactivity, not aging alone.

On average, we reach peak muscle mass somewhere between 20 and 30, then lose about 8% per decade after that. By the time many adults reach their 70s and 80s, they may have only 60–80% of the muscle mass they had at 30.

A big reason why is anabolic resistance. As we get older, muscle becomes less responsive to amino acids, one of the key signals for building and maintaining muscle.

This is where resistance training becomes non-negotiable. It’s one of the main signals that tells muscle to grow. And just as importantly, it helps re-sensitize muscle to amino acids, so the body responds to protein more like it did when you were younger.

caption:
A SIMPLE WAY TO REFLEXIVELY ENGAGE DIAPHRAGMATIC NASAL BREATHING (WHICH HAS VARIOUS HEALTH BENEFITS IN WAKING & SLEEP) 

For a number of years, my laboratory @stanford.med in collaboration w/Spiegel Lab also @stanford explored how different patterns of breathing impacted mental state, sleep, resting heart rate, heart rate variability, and other metrics both during and for many hours after those specific patterns of breathing were completed. 

That study letter to various conclusions, including that basically all forms of deliberate breath work done for about five minutes are beneficial in some way or another, and in particular repeated (cyclic) physiological sighs (double inhale via nose then long to lungs empty exhale) 
doi.org/10.1016/j.xcrm.2022.100895 

Over the years, it’s also become clear that while breathwork has its benefits, there’s also great benefit to proper breathing mechanics in sleep (to avoid apnea) and while waking (1-3 physiological sighs for instance to rapidly decrease stress). 

Some years ago @_brianmackenzie a pioneer in human performance talked to me about the “pull breath back not up” when trying to engage the diaphragm. This works particularly well when stressed or fatigued. The reason is that stress can often lead to shortness of breath and breathing in this way allows you to obtain a really deep breath in no small part because the nasal passage is (generally) deeper parallel to the roof of your mouth than it is vertically.

Note: people with deviated septum’s often find they can do this whereas other forms of deliberate nasal breathing are difficult for them.

And I want to acknowledge that essentially all forms of deliberate breathing can be found and described first in Yogic practices. No one has trademark or domain over breathing!

The source vs symptom framing is the right one. Chronic low-grade inflammation rarely starts on its own, it is usually downstream of a few drivers running quietly: visceral fat acting as an endocrine organ that pumps out IL-6 and TNF-alpha, a leaky gut barrier letting LPS into circulation (metabolic endotoxemia), and short sleep, which on its own raises CRP the next morning. They mostly converge on the same switch, NF-kB. hsCRP and IL-6 are the cheap markers that make it visible. Lowering the number without touching the driver is just turning down the smoke alarm. 🧠

Hitting a wall during your workouts? Getting that awful afternoon brain fog that coffee just can't fix? It might be time to look at what's happening inside your body, specifically, your iron levels. 🏃‍♀️📉

Why tracking this matters for your energy:
🍽️ Iron helps your body turn the food you eat into real, usable energy.
📉Low iron means you get tired faster, your heart has to work harder, and it takes longer to recover after a tough workout.
🎯Your brain needs constant oxygen to think clearly. When iron is low, it’s much harder to focus.

➡️If you are already tracking your sleep, your steps, and your food, make sure you are tracking your blood data, too. Getting healthy always starts from the inside out. 🩸✨

caption:
DELIBERATELY LENGTHENING 1 EXHALE JUST 8-10X DAY INCREASES YOUR HEART RATE VARIABILITY (A VERY GOOD THING FOR HEALTH) •
-
We hear lot these days about HRV: heart rate variability. In general, increased HRV is a reflection of a healthy autonomic nervous system because it means that your vagus nerve efferents (outputs) to your heart are acting to decelerate and counteract your sympathetic nervous system. 
-
The best way to conceptualize this is that it reflects a capacity that you have to “push back” on any tendency for your autonomic system to veer too far into a stressed mode. 
-
Exhales done deliberately, in particular when you extend their duration and/or intensity, activate a branch of your vagus nerve that goes from your brain to your heart, and because of something called respiratory sinus arrhythmia, they slow your HR down. 
-
During this weeks Huberman lab podcast I describe a brain circuit that extends from the your forebrain DLPFC all the way down to the heart and that directly involves vagus nerve control over your autonomic nervous system.
-
Note: what is recommended in the slide does not mean that you have to do 10 long exhales repeatedly! It just means that every once in a while in your day if you just deliberately extend an exhale you’ll notice an increase in HRV. 
-
This DLPFC-INSULA-VAGAL-HEART circuit is prone to plasticity and doing it deliberately will increase its engagement both and sleep and spontaneously throughout the day.
-
I explain more about the incredible structure and function of the vagus nerve, including its role in regulating serotonin levels in the brain & more during the episode.
-

caption:
Should you exercise fasted or fed? It depends on whether you’re a man or a woman.

Men can get away with training on empty. Women can’t. 

When women exercise without eating first, their bodies produce more stress hormones, blunt the post-workout recovery signals, and miss the window where the real benefits happen. The minimum energy threshold for women to function without dysfunction is more than double that of men.

You don’t need a full meal. You just need something. @drstacysims makes a cold protein latte the night before (espresso, almond milk, a scoop of protein) and drinks it on the way to the gym.

And whatever you do, don’t replace real food with protein Cheerios or a Dunkin protein shake. The food industry has mastered the art of slapping the word protein on things that have no business being called food. Read the ingredient list. 

If you can’t pronounce it or find it in your kitchen, put it back.

Full conversation with Dr. Stacy Sims is out now on The Dr. Hyman Show Podcast.

Нам не хватает способности любить, ёмкости впустить любовь не хватает. 
Мы оперируем на ёмкости малышей. Мы зависли в тех программах. Малыш, когда сталкивается с сопротивлением, начинает плакать от обиды или топать ножками и махать кулачками. У него просто нет другой операционной системы, он ограничен в силу своего естественного уровня развития. Часто во взрослой жизни мы ведомы той же операционной системой, как трехлетка или пятилетка. Чуть что, мы либо куксимся и внутренне плачем либо ругаемся и требуем своего. Нам не хватает способностей взрослого человека посмотреть на проблему через мудрость, а главное - через любовь. Любовь к себе и к другому.
Представьте ситуацию, где вам нахамили, что вы сразу сделаете или подумаете ? Фу, хам, правильно?
Там сразу включится сопротивление, которое вынудит вас или отстраниться самому или устранить "хама".  Но на самом деле вам бы подойти к хаму, как взрослый подошел бы к трехлетннму карапузу. Что бы вы сказали и сделали  такому? Ну явно не куксились бы и не обижались, просто не вступили бы в конфронтацию с ним.
Мы обижаемся, когда нам не хватает ёмкости для любви. Когда мы сами оперируем как малыш.
Нам не хватает ни мыслей, ни слов, ни поступков, продиктованных любовью к себе и к другому. В первую очередь к себе. Проявив любовь к себе, мы даём пример другим. И затем проявляя любовь/доброту к другому мы помогаем ему обогатить его операционный арсенал. 
Только так человек учится увеличивать свою емкость любви. Ведь малыш не умеет этого делать. Не обладает этими способностями. Его эмоциональный интеллект еще не до конца развит.
Вот так мы и ходим, эмоциональные карапузы в телах дядь и тёть, недоразвитиые. Куксимся, плачем, топаем ножками и машем кулачками. А что надо делать? Правильно, надо проявлять любовь. Легко сказать, да трудно сделать. Не так ли? Против программы не попрешь, а надо.
Надо все время преодолевать в себе и в других того малыша. Точнее надо его любить, но только любовью мудрого взрослого. 
Вспомните последние неприятные ситуации. Посмотрите на них с этой точки зрения. Что вы увидите? Кто проявился как карапуз? Вы или они, или вы оба?

We lack the ability to love, the capacity for love. We operate on the capacity of children. We're stuck in those same programs. A child, when confronted with resistance, starts crying or stamping their feet and waving their fists in frustration. They simply don't have another operating system; they're limited by their natural level of development. Often, in adulthood, we're driven by the same operating system as a three- or five-year-old. At the slightest mishap, we either sulk and cry internally, or we demand our way. We lack the adult ability to look at the problem through wisdom, and most importantly, through love. Love, first for yourself, and second for others.
Imagine a situation where someone is rude to you. What would you do or think? Resistance would immediately kick in, right? But in reality, you should approach them the way an adult would approach a three-year-old. What would you say and do to such a person? Well, you certainly wouldn't sulk or take offense, and wouldn't enter into confrontation with them.
We take offense when we lack the capacity for love. When we operate like a toddler.
We lack thoughts, words, and actions motivated by love for ourselves and for others. First and foremost, for ourselves. By showing love for ourselves, we set an example for others. And then, by showing love and kindness to others, we help them expand their operational arsenal.
Only in this way can a person learn to increase their capacity for love. After all, a toddler can't do this. They don't possess these abilities. Their emotional intelligence is not yet fully developed.
So that's how we go about, emotional toddlers in the bodies of uncles and aunties, underdeveloped. We sulk, cry loudly, stamp our feet, and wave our fists. But what should we do?  That's right, we need to show love. Easy said, hard done, right? You can't go against the program, but we must.
We must constantly overcome that little one in ourselves and in others. More precisely, we must love them, but only with the love of a wise adult.
Recall the last unpleasant situations. Look at them from this perspective. What do you see? Who showed up as the little one? You or them, or both of you?

caption:
A “plastic-free diet” can cut endocrine-disrupting chemicals in the body by up to 60% in just 1 week.

Participants in a recent study switched to low-plastic food, plastic-free kitchenware, and screened personal care products for 7 days.

Urinary BPA fell by 59%, and phthalates fell by up to 54%. Even switching personal care products alone significantly lowered MnBP, another phthalate, by 35%.

These chemicals have been linked to male and female reproductive problems, altered neurodevelopment in children, and even insulin resistance and cardiovascular disease.

The takeaway here is that exposure to plastic is not fixed or unavoidable. Reducing highly processed foods, canned foods, plastic packaging, and plastic contact during food prep and storage, as well as personal hygiene products that contain phthalates, can rapidly lower your internal burden of these chemicals.

Study title: Low-plastic diet and urinary levels of plastic-associated phthalates and bisphenols: the randomized controlled PERTH Trial

caption:
FIX/SET YOUR CORTISOL RHYTHM: THE FIRST KEY STEP 

Few biological mechanisms have more of an impact on how we feel than cortisol. We all have a natural rhythm in cortisol whereby it rises and drops across the 24 hour cycle.

There are unique time windows when we can amplify or suppress cortisol. These have major impact on how we feel during the day and how we sleep at night as well as on our mood and cognition.

For a variety of reasons, many people nowadays suffer from having cortisol too low in the morning and too high in the evening. Fixing this is a multi step process, but one of the major things that everyone can do easily that is safe and zero cost is to view bright light, ideally from sunlight, first thing in the morning. 

As the slide points out, if you don’t have access to sunlight you can purchase a 10,000 Lux artificial light. (I have no relationship to any company that sells these.)

It’s still a good idea to get sunlight in your eyes once the sun is out but keep in mind that the first hour upon waking is a unique time window where you can amplify cortisol, which has the dual effective, raising your energy levels, metabolism, and mood in the day and setting you up for lower cortisol at night so you can sleep well.

People with Cushing’s syndrome of course should not spike their cortisol. However, they are recommended to regulate their circadian patterns and cortisol just like anyone else.

There’s more to say about this topic that I’m covering in an upcoming episode of the Huberman podcast, but in the meantime, just this one simple step can have an outsized positive effect for everyone.

Yes, it still works on cloudy days. No don’t wear sunglasses when doing it. Eyeglasses and contacts are fine. Blink as needed to protect your eyes. Never stare at the sun or any bright light. 

Meanwhile, if you have any questions or comments about this or other topics (or guests you’d like to see me to host on the Huberman lab podcast), please put them in the comments section below.

caption:
HOW TO GET MORE DEEP SLEEP •
-
Sleep is the foundation of mental health, physical health and performance. Sleep includes multiple stages. Two of the most important stages are slow wave deep sleep, and REM: rapid eye movement sleep.
-
The first 3-4 hours after falling asleep are when you can get the most slow wave deep sleep. It’s also associated with growth hormone release in the first two hours. 
-
The slide above explains what you can do to help yourself get the best and most deep sleep. Closer to morning you’ll start to explain more rapid movement sleep.
-
Even though it’s best not to eat anything two hours prior to sleep, don’t try and fall asleep with gnawing hunger. Better to eat a small snack than to struggle to sleep due to hunger. 
-
Slow wave sleep is a lower metabolic state, it requires low blood glucose levels. Rapid movement sleep is actually a state of very high brain activity, even more than in waking.
-
In a future post, I’ll cover ways to improve rapid eye movement sleep, but in general it’s supported by heating your sleeping environment as opposed to cooling it. 
-
